external_invariants: Model: GPT2LMHeadModel with n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024, resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0, use_cache=False, attn_implementation='eager', FP32, train mode, initialized immediately after torch.manual_seed(20261020).

Data: per-rank synthetic token IDs drawn with torch.Generator().manual_seed(31000 + rank); accumulation_steps=4 tensors of shape (micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128) with values in [0, 50257); no other dataset exists (request assets are empty by design).

Numerics: FP32 end to end; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False; torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False; torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False; torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest'); no autocast, no GradScaler, no compilation.

Accumulation: optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) at step start; loss for each micro-batch is model(input_ids=tokens, labels=tokens, use_cache=False).loss / 4; first 3 micro-batches run under DDP no_sync, only the final micro-batch triggers gradient synchronization; reported loss is the sum of the 4 scaled micro losses and must be finite.

Optimizer: SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False); exactly one optimizer.step() per workload repetition; SGD keeps no momentum state so the reset only reloads the initial weights.

DDP configuration: broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, device_ids=[bound device index]; find_unused_parameters stays False; no communication hooks are registered in the measured path (the source registers its inventory hook only in a separate diagnostic step).

Cross-rank semantics: after the final micro-batch every rank holds bitwise-identical gradients (source exact_gradient_replica_check with atol=0, rtol=0); effective global batch = world_size 2 x micro_batch 1 x accumulation_steps 4 = 8 micro-batches = 1024 tokens per step.
Reset fidelity: every repetition starts from the same initial weights (CPU state_dict snapshot), empty gradients, empty optimizer state and the prepare-time RNG states.

Timing hygiene: control coordination (barrier, peak-memory reset, synchronization) uses the separate gloo group and happens outside the timer; the only NCCL collectives in the measured workload are the DDP gradient allreduces of the final accumulation micro-batch; step_ms must stay <= 1.05x baseline.

Observations: loss, per-micro losses, every gradient tensor and every updated parameter of the ~124M-parameter model are exposed as full tensors; no elapsed times or performance counters appear in observations.
Quality scope: gradient/parameter comparisons use atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-4 (request.quality); reference fidelity only, no downstream accuracy or convergence claim.

Workload frozen: batch, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4, world_size=2, architecture, FP32 precision, seeded data, completion boundary and quality checks are never altered to improve a score.

selection.rationale: The project objective is step_ms (clean original baseline 140.41/140.69 ms) with a secondary minimum on diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms. The only NCCL work inside the measured boundary is the final accumulation micro-batch's DDP gradient allreduce, and it dominates observed device time: 13 c10d::allreduce_ invocations per rank, exactly covering the 124,439,808-element gradient as 12 buckets of 7,087,872 elements (28.35 MB each) plus one 39,385,344-element embedding bucket (wte+wpe+ln_f, 157.5 MB, 6.3x the 25 MB bucket cap). Rank 0's NCCL kernel sum is 58.92 ms (39.44 ms over the 12 small buckets at ~8.6 GB/s effective, 19.48 ms for the giant bucket at ~8.1 GB/s) while rank 1 shows 210.82 ms; the ~152 ms difference is spin-wait from discovery-hook rank skew, not wire time, so the wire-equivalent communication cost is ~59 ms per rank. Every collective runs ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL - the low-bandwidth LL protocol - even for the 157.5 MB bucket that becomes ready last and is fully exposed after backward finishes, and the 13-way split adds per-call ring latency and serializes the flush. Non-communication kernels sum to only ~34 ms (rank 0) / ~39 ms (rank 1) per step, so a large share of the 140 ms clean step is exposed communication, making this the biggest lever on both step_ms and the communication diagnostic. The two groups are one mechanism - the DDP reducer's bucket flush at the final micro-batch - and cannot be edited independently, so they form a joint candidate at a single coherent editable boundary (how the final gradient synchronization executes in the project source): coarsening/fusing the flush into fewer, larger contiguous allreduces and/or steering these transfers off the LL protocol. For world_size=2 every gradient element is a single two-operand sum regardless of bucket grouping or NCCL protocol, so cross-rank bitwise-identical gradients, the atol=1e-6/rtol=1e-4 reference checks and the frozen workload semantics are preserved.
selection.hypothesis: Restructuring the final-sync execution at these two allreduce call sites - fewer, larger contiguous allreduce(s) over the same gradient bytes (and/or SIMPLE-protocol-sized transfers instead of RING_LL) - will cut the per-rank NCCL kernel sum from ~59 ms toward the ~16 GB/s interconnect floor (~31 ms) and shrink exposed tail latency, measurably reducing step_ms below the 140.4/140.7 ms baseline (trivially satisfying the <=1.05x cap for the communication goal) with gradients and updated parameters unchanged within quality tolerances. This is a hypothesis to be tested with the paired-repeats measurement and the separately collected diagnostic objective, not an accepted benefit: the clean-timing exposure may differ from the hook-perturbed profile, and a negative or neutral step_ms result should be reported as measured.

proposal.rationale: The two selected sites are the DDP reducer's per-bucket c10d::allreduce_ calls of the final accumulation micro-batch: 12 invocations of the 7,087,872-element transformer bucket (d0938de87369efd500322679) plus 1 invocation of the 39,385,344-element embedding bucket (b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b), the complete 497,759,232 gradient bytes per rank. Observed structure on these ranks: every one of the 13 collectives runs ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_f32_RING_LL on 2 channels over the SHM transport (the validation-run NCCL log shows 'Channel 00/01 -> 1 via SHM/direct/direct', network Socket; the source's own record shows can_device_access_peer false, so no P2P/NVLink claim is made), moving ~59 ms of wire time per rank in the clean baseline (rank 0 kernel sum 39.44 + 19.48 ms) at ~8.1-8.6 GB/s useful payload per direction, consistent with LL's flag-byte overhead halving the useful rate of the host-bounce path; the sibling project's capability collection on these same two devices recorded GPU 1's PCIe link at gen 4 x8 current (GPU 0 x16), which bounds the useful Simple-protocol rate at roughly 12-13 GB/s per direction and the allreduce floor near ~40 ms. The candidate therefore attacks the one transport lever that does not touch workload semantics: the NCCL protocol actually used for these 13 flush calls. Every invocation keeps real in-place SUM semantics on the same bucket tensor and returns a live Work produced by a real ProcessGroupNCCL allreduce (work.boxed(), the exact ABI that passed quality with zero gradient error in the sibling project's parent routing); what changes is only which NCCL communicator executes it. In route=adaptive (default) build() directly constructs a fresh ProcessGroupNCCL over a uniquely prefixed view of the default group's store (a fresh ncclCommInitRank, not a comm split, so communicator-level tuning is not inherited) inside an NCCL_PROTO=Simple environment window that is restored before build returns, warms it with a guarded one-element allreduce, and then times one bucket-sized (7,087,872-element fp32) allreduce on both the default backend and the fresh backend with CUDA events; a gloo control-group consensus (no NCCL kernels) sums both ranks' microsecond timings and build status, and every rank routes all 13 flush calls of every step onto the fresh communicator only if the aggregate fresh timing is at least 5% faster with every rank's build healthy - otherwise every rank keeps the parent path. route=parent reproduces the baseline routing exactly and is an explicit point of the parameter space so the search can measure the null in-band. How the prior sibling feedback changes this attempt: (1) the leaf-a project's tuned-communicator trials regressed step_ms from ~147 ms to ~245-261 ms with NCCL_ALGO=Tree forced, min/max CTA overrides of 8-32 channels, an optional high-priority stream, and only the 12 small buckets moved (leaving the 157.5 MB embedding bucket interleaving on a second stream); this candidate forces no algorithm, leaves NCCL's channel defaults untouched, uses the ordinary-priority stream, and moves all 13 calls together so the measured path has exactly one active communicator and the same 13-collective sequential structure as the baseline, with the probe gate demoting the whole mechanism if the fresh communicator is not genuinely faster on this box; (2) the p5 project's ProcessGroupNCCL coalescing wrapper (_start_coalescing/_end_coalescing) executed with exact cross-rank gradients but failed reference quality deterministically on the wte gradient (8.8e-6 > 1e-6), so no grouping, deferral or coalescing is used here - each call is issued and completed independently; (3) the p5 staged-scratch design crashed on the op's Work cast because the reducer consumes work->getFuture() result tensors per bucket, so no synthetic, cached or foreign Work is ever minted here. Expected effect and honesty: if Simple over this host-bounce path roughly doubles the useful rate (LL flag overhead removed), the ~59 ms flush drops toward ~40 ms and step_ms falls materially below the 140.4/140.7 ms baseline; if NCCL's tuner is already right for SHM, the probe ties or loses and the candidate degrades to the parent path with no gain and no semantic change - the improvement claim is submitted as a hypothesis for the paired-repeats measurement, not as an observed fact. Gradient and parameter correctness are structurally preserved: for world_size=2 the reduction is exactly one commutative fp32 addition per element regardless of communicator or protocol, so cross-rank gradients stay bitwise identical (the source's atol=0 replica check) and the 1e-6/1e-4 reference comparisons see the same values as the baseline, exactly as the sibling project's quality pass on a tuned communicator demonstrated.

steps: build() reads state/device/rank/world_size, the observed bucket element counts from context['targets'] signatures (7,087,872 and 39,385,344, with hardcoded fallbacks), and the tunable route from context['parameters'] (default 'adaptive').

route=adaptive first call per process: construct a fresh ProcessGroupNCCL(PrefixStore(unique tag, default group's store), rank, world_size, Options) with a 60 s timeout, inside an NCCL_PROTO=Simple environment window; force its communicator initialization with a one-element fp32 allreduce guarded by a 30 s wait; restore the environment in a finally block before returning, so no other communicator initialization observes the window.

Paired probe outside any measured boundary: one warmup plus two timed 7,087,872-element fp32 allreduces (CUDA events, best-of-two) on the default NCCL backend and on the fresh backend, executed in the same order on every rank; the probe tensor is freed afterwards.

Consensus: a 3-element int64 tensor [build_status, default_us, fresh_us] is all-reduced over the adapter's gloo control group; both ranks compute the identical decision (route to the fresh communicator iff every rank's build is healthy and the summed default timing exceeds 1.05x the summed fresh timing). Any local failure, non-CUDA device, missing control group or probe anomaly demotes every rank to the parent path, so collective participation and routing stay symmetric.

The decision and communicator are cached under a process-unique sys.modules key so repeated installs in one worker process (quality, coverage, measurement) reuse one communicator and one probe instead of accumulating them; route=parent never consults or writes the cache.

Each of the two call sites returns a closure that, for a compatible signature (single contiguous 1-D fp32 CUDA bucket tensor of a known size, sparse_indices None, async call), issues the real in-place SUM allreduce on the chosen backend and returns (tensors, work.boxed()); every other shape, dtype, stride, sync or sparse invocation falls back to the parent c10d::allreduce_ op through context['references'].
setup_work.memory: Setup allocates one transient 28.35 MB fp32 probe tensor (freed after the probe) and constructs one additional NCCL communicator per rank, retained for the process lifetime: its channel buffers and internal state are driver allocations not visible to torch's caching-allocator counters, on the order of tens of MiB per rank, reported here rather than claimed as a saving. If the probe demotes, the already-initialized communicator is abandoned but kept referenced by the cache so at most one extra communicator exists per process. No CUDA Graphs are captured and no torch pools are introduced, so framework.peak_allocated_bytes/reserved counters are expected unchanged apart from the transient build-time probe; lifecycle peaks can only grow by that transient setup allocation.
setup_work.timing_scope: All construction, probing and consensus runs inside build(), before validation and measurement, outside the declared workload boundary; the measured run() still executes four forward/backward micro-batches, all 13 gradient allreduces of the final micro-batch (each a real NCCL collective of the same bytes and semantics), exactly one optimizer.step() and the closing synchronization. No call is eliminated; the flush's collective count, order and payloads are unchanged.

quality_risks: The ReduceOp argument of c10d::allreduce_ is a boxed ScriptObject that cannot be introspected from Python, so the fresh path reconstructs AllreduceOptions with ReduceOp.SUM; this matches every observed invocation (the DDP default hook with no communication hooks registered in the measured path), and a hypothetical non-SUM call would fail the exact-gradient and reference checks loudly rather than silently.

Cross-rank routing symmetry is required for collective matching: guaranteed by identical build() sequences on both ranks, a shared per-build PrefixStore tag, and the gloo consensus that demotes all ranks on any local build/probe failure; the decision is computed once per process and cached, so later installs cannot diverge from earlier ones.

If NCCL_PROTO=Simple is unsupported for this transport the fresh communicator's initialization raises and the candidate degrades to the exact parent path; if Simple initializes but is slower than LL, the 1.05x probe margin demotes it; if the probe is unrepresentative of in-step behavior the paired measurement and the workload's 1.05x step_ms cap bound the damage to a rejected candidate rather than a corrupted result.

Gradient and parameter fidelity: for world_size=2 the SUM is one commutative fp32 addition per element independent of communicator, protocol or channel count, so cross-rank gradients remain bitwise identical (atol=0 replica check) and the 1e-6/1e-4 reference comparisons observe baseline values; the sibling project's quality pass with a differently-tuned NCCL communicator on this same workload (0.0 max_abs_error over 248,879,623 compared elements across two continuous steps) is direct prior evidence, with residual protocol-level reduction-order effects impossible for two operands.

The 5%-probe margin and best-of-two timing make accidental switching on noise unlikely, and an accidental switch is still semantics-preserving; the retained extra communicator's driver memory is not reclaimed until process exit and is not measured by the framework's torch memory counters.

NCCL environment mutation is confined to the fresh communicator's construction-and-init window and restored in a finally block; the default communicator, the gloo control group and any later communicator initialization observe the original environment.

The framework's TorchDispatchMode-level signature guard plus the candidate's own guards mean unexpected shapes, dtypes, strides, sync calls or sparse indices execute the parent op unchanged, so partial coverage degrades to baseline behavior instead of incorrect reductions.

params.name: route
params.description: parent: every invocation of both call sites dispatches to the parent c10d::allreduce_ op on the workload's default NCCL communicator (bit-identical baseline routing, the in-band null point). adaptive: build-time paired probe times one bucket-sized allreduce on the default backend and on a freshly initialized NCCL communicator whose ncclCommInitRank runs inside an NCCL_PROTO=Simple environment window (restored before build returns); a gloo control-group consensus routes all 13 flush calls of every step onto the fresh communicator only when it is at least 5% faster in aggregate with every rank's build healthy, otherwise all ranks keep the parent path. Both values preserve per-call in-place SUM semantics, real NCCL collectives, bitwise-identical two-rank gradients and the frozen workload.
